title: Dedicated capacity weekly prep - 2026-03-07
content:
Goal: prep for weekly dedicated capacity sync (core topics: GPU pool utilization, reservations update, autoscaling policy tuning, upcoming renewals).

Agenda (10:00am PT, 30m):
- Quick numbers snapshot (2m)
- Reservations & renewal requests (7m)
- Autoscaling behavior & hot-path latency incidents (7m)
- Forecast and demand signal (7m)
- Action items & blockers (7m)

Snapshot (last 7 days):
- Total reserved GPUs: 420 (across 6 pools)
- Avg utilization across reserved pools: 68% (up from 61% last week)
- Peak per-pool utilization: pool-delta-gpu-a = 94% (sustained 30m window), pool-epsilon-gpu-b = 88%
- On-demand (hosted) spillover: avg 12% of requests routed to hosted API due to capacity constraints
- Cost note: reserved utilization improvement reduced per-token GPU cost estimate by ~8% MoM

Open reservations / renewals: 
- ACME Corp long-term: requested +120 GPUs (A100) for Q2 start date 2026-04-01. Request in sales pipeline; legal needs SOW. (JIRA-DCAP-87)
- RetailCo burst window: needs guaranteed burst capacity for Black Friday-style test on 2026-06-15; propose 48 GPUs reserved with autoscale buffer.
- Internal infra team: ask to convert 32 unassigned GPUs in pool-theta into a short-term reservation (3 months) to support evals.

Autoscaling behavior notes:
- Recent incident (2026-03-04): autoscaler failed to spin additional nodes for pool-delta when burst exceeded threshold due to bad instance filter (tag mismatch). Consequence: latency spike ~300ms P90 for webhooks; most requests fell back to hosted.
  - Root cause: instance template changed name by release-engineering -> autoscaler filter didn't match new name (see PR #421).
  - Fix deployed 2026-03-05: template name reconciled; autoscaler tests added to CI.
  - Follow-up: add alert for "scale-request-failed" events and a dashboard panel that surfaces instance-template drift. Owner: Alex Morgan.

Forecast / demand signal:
- Pipeline leading indicators: 3 enterprise deals >100 GPUs likely to close in Apr-May (probability-weighted +205 GPUs).
- Internal ML eval windows scheduled mid-April for finetune campaigns (~60 GPU-days) -> temporary bump in short-term demand.
- Model onboarding: plan to add two Llama2-70B variants to hosted catalog; expected higher memory + lower throughput -> estimate +18% reserved GPU-seconds for similar traffic.

Decisions to make in meeting:
- Prioritize ACME request: commit to start date 2026-04-01? If yes, we need 120 GPUs reserved by 2026-03-20 to secure capacity.
- Convert unassigned pool-theta GPUs for internal evals or leave for opportunistic bookings? (ops prefers reservation to avoid fragmentation)
- Autoscaler threshold tuning: move conservative thresholds to aggressive for low-latency tiers (impact on cost).

Risks / unknowns:
- Spot market volatility in late Q2 could reduce available capacity for new reservations -> consider earlier procurement for enterprise deals.
- Model quantization progress (Optimize team) may change GPU-hours per request estimates next month -> forecasts likely to be conservative until we validate.

Notes-to-self / talking points:
- Emphasize that utilization uptrend is healthy but peak saturation events indicate we still need buffer for SLOs.
- Recommend 10% reserved buffer for latency-sensitive pools; propose temp buffer shift from non-critical pools.
- Ask sales to push ACME to sign SOW by 2026-03-18; provide draft SOW link in chat.

Action items (pre-meeting / assign):
- [Maya] Create quick deck with 1-slide utilization + 1-slide forecast (due by 09:30am)
- [Alex] Add "scale-request-failed" alert + dashboard panel (in-progress)
- [Ryan] Confirm ACME POC timeline with sales and share legal SOW blocker list
- [Jenna] Validate pool-theta inventory and list exact GPU serials that could be reassigned
- [Infra] Run smoke test for autoscaler templates across regions (scheduled 2026-03-09)

Follow-ups (post-meeting):
- Capture decision on ACME reservation & set procurement timeline
- If convert pool-theta, schedule migrations during low-util window (propose 03/28 - 03/30)
- Update capacity model spreadsheet (link to sheet in linked artifacts) with new committed GPUs and revised cost forecasts

Draft messages: 
- To Sales (ACME): "We can commit to a 120-GPU reservation starting 2026-04-01 conditional on signed SOW by 2026-03-18. If we move forward I'll send procurement timelines and onboarding checklist."
- To Infra Ops: "We saw template naming drift that impacted autoscaling; please ensure any instance template rename includes an autoscaler tag alias. Adding a CI job to catch this going forward."

Misc notes / scratchpad:
- Quick calc: if ACME 120 GPUs reserved -> incremental monthly cost estimate ~$140k (back-of-envelope) — need finance to confirm.
- If we pre-procure for Q2 enterprise deals, cost vs lost revenue tradeoff: option A) pre-procure 200 GPUs for Apr-May, tie to short-term internal usage for slack -> reduces risk of losing deals but increases committed spend.

Questions for manager (1:1 follow-up):
- Approve pre-procurement for 200 GPUs to cover high-prob pipeline? (ask for risk appetite)
- Policy preference: keep 10% buffer for low-latency pools or let autoscaler handle (we've seen autoscaler edge cases).

References & links:
- Confluence: dedicated capacity plan (CONFLUENCE-1234-dedicated-gpu-plan)
- JIRA: JIRA-DCAP-87, JIRA-DCAP-102 (autoscaler fixes)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/421

End of notes.

TODO (personal): tidy slides, drop 2 charts into deck (utilization trend, forecast table), ping legal about SOW template.
